findings.claim: The declared Python floor is wrong, so setup fails for a learner who meets the stated prerequisite. README line 45, lab.json prerequisites ("3.10 or later") and tests/setup_python.mjs line 23 (minor >= 10) all accept Python 3.10. But tests/requirements.txt pins starlette==1.10.0 and annotated-doc==0.0.7, and their installed METADATA in the lab venv says Requires-Python >=3.11 (all other pins accept 3.10). Reproduced: a pip dry-run of tests/requirements.txt with --python-version 3.10 --only-binary=:all: fails with "Ignored the following versions that require a different python version: 0.0.7 Requires-Python >=3.11 ... No matching distribution found for annotated-doc==0.0.7"; the same run with 3.11 resolves all 14 pins. Python 3.10 is the default python3 on Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, so this is a learner a Standard cohort will plausibly include. setup_python.mjs passes its own version check, creates .venv with 3.10, then pip fails with that message, which contradicts the README; no troubleshooting line covers it. Recovery is also blocked: setup_python.mjs line 29 creates the venv only when .venv's python is missing, so after the learner installs a newer Python and reruns npm run setup, the old 3.10 venv is reused and pip fails again. Reproduced the reuse with a venv created --without-pip: rerunning setup reuses it and exits 1 ("No module named pip") without recreating it. The learner is stuck until they delete .venv, which nothing tells them; tests 24-26 cannot pass, so the lab cannot be completed.
findings.recommendation: Make the floor match the pins: say Python 3.11 or later in README line 45, lab.json prerequisites and the troubleshooting line, and require minor >= 11 in setup_python.mjs line 23. Alternatively, pin versions that support 3.10, if the module's FastAPI/Starlette pins allow it. In setup_python.mjs, check the existing .venv's interpreter version (and that pip imports), and recreate .venv when it is too old or broken. Add a troubleshooting line: if setup fails after changing Python, delete .venv and rerun npm run setup.

findings.claim: Tests 24-26 print false "no HTTPX call" messages for two plausible mistakes, so the feedback sends the learner the wrong way. (1) README phase 4 rule 2 (line 88) asks for "an httpx.Timeout with a 2-second connect limit and a 3-second read limit". The natural reading, httpx.Timeout(connect=2.0, read=3.0), raises ValueError ("httpx.Timeout must either include a default, or set all four parameters explicitly.", checked in the lab venv). Written inside the handler, as the starter's call is, it makes tests 24, 25 and 26 fail with "got 500 (an exception escaped unhandled) and the service made no HTTPX call to the shop api ... call the api with httpx, as the starter does", "... never called the shop api: make the call" and "... never called it ... make the call to the shop api with httpx". The learner did write the httpx call, and the real cause is never shown. The same Timeout built at module level gets an excellent message ("could not be loaded: ValueError: httpx.Timeout must either include a default ..."), so the information exists but only reaches the learner for one placement. (2) A call that writes the compose value http://api:8080 into the URL, instead of building it from API_BASE_URL, gets 200 and the same three "made no HTTPX call" messages. The stand-in did record the call; it is filtered out by the API_BASE_URL prefix (shopCalls, line 228), and the message never says which URL was called or which was expected. Both are one-edit slips on the README path.
findings.recommendation: In tests/service_behavior.py, record the exception type and message of an unhandled server error for each scenario (for example with raise_server_exceptions=True inside a try, or an exception hook), and have lab.mjs print it when a scenario got an unhandled 500 ("... raised ValueError: httpx.Timeout must either include a default ..."). When outgoing requests exist but none starts with API_BASE_URL, say so: "the service called <url>, not the API_BASE_URL it was given: build the URL from API_BASE_URL". Keep "made no HTTPX call" for when OUTGOING is empty and no exception was recorded.

findings.claim: lab.json was not updated for the Python setup and now contradicts the README and the contract. (a) cleanup.paths (lines 126-129) lists only tests/node_modules and starter/.env. The lab now creates .venv next to the README (README lines 53 and 135; setup_python.mjs line 9). lab-contract.md section 7 requires lab.json to declare every path the lab creates. (b) cleanup.notes (line 130) still says "Delete tests/node_modules ... and starter/.env" and "nothing runs a container engine, Python or any pipeline". Tests 24-26 now run Python, and tests 6-7 run workflow steps under bash. (c) licensing (line 152) says fastapi and httpx are "never installed or executed by this lab, only read as text". npm run setup now installs and imports them plus twelve other pinned packages from tests/requirements.txt (starlette, pydantic, pydantic_core, anyio, certifi, idna, h11, httpcore, typing_extensions, typing-inspection, annotated-types, annotated-doc), and none of those has a licence record. A learner or platform owner reading lab.json, the declarative manifest the platform handoff uses, gets a false cleanup list and a false description of what runs on their machine.
findings.recommendation: Add ".venv" to cleanup.paths. Rewrite cleanup.notes to match README line 135: Python and bash run locally against stand-ins, and no container engine or pipeline runs. Replace the fastapi/httpx licensing entry with one entry per package installed from tests/requirements.txt, giving its licence and source, and stating that setup installs it into .venv and the tests import it, uncommitted. Confirm each licence from its PyPI page with a retrieval date in evidence.

findings.claim: Loop 5 regression of ops-edu-r1-01 item (2). The new test 24 message for a call with all limits off includes a parenthetical stating what timeout=None does to the limits. The shipped starter passes timeout=None, so this message prints on the phase 1 run. It answers worksheet field service_calls.httpx_with_timeout_none (decisions.yaml line 66), which phase 5 asks later and which the reconciled acceptance says must be decided from the service-to-service page, not from any starter-run message. The loop-4 message only pointed to the page. Because the loop-2 reconciliation closed ops-edu-11 on the proviso that no reworded timeout message singles out a worksheet option, ops-edu-11 reopens too. Reproduced on the starter run (see the ops-edu-r1-01 recheck item). The expected option itself is not repeated here.
findings.recommendation: Reword the starter-run branch (tests/lab.mjs line 240) to name the rule without its conclusion, as loop 4 did, for example: "the call to the shop api passes timeout=None: reread what the service-to-service page says that does, then pass an httpx.Timeout with a 2-second connect limit and a 3-second read limit". The other branches (lines 241-242) print only after a learner edit and may stay.

findings.claim: Test 7 ("no step prints a secret to the run log") recognises only the whole value, base64 and hex (leaks(), lines 451-466). A secret-seeing step that prints the value transformed or in part passes 26/26. Reproduced with an env-mapped REGISTRY_PASSWORD piped through rev, and through sed inserting a space after each character, beside the README login. By inspection of leaks(), a substring print such as ${REGISTRY_PASSWORD:0:N} is not matched either, because only whole-value forms are searched. The secrets page the test points to teaches exactly this weakness: redaction misses a value that is reworded or written backwards (secrets-in-ci/artifact.md line 65), and an exact-text filter cannot be the security boundary (line 67). So the lab's own check shares the flaw the page warns about. Off the README path, which says to delete the debugging output; hence low.
findings.recommendation: Optional: in leaks(), also match the reversed value, the value with whitespace removed from the log, and any substring of the made-up secret's random part of, say, 6 or more characters (the made-up values are lab-...-<hex tag>, so the tag is the part to search for). Or state in README line 118 that test 7 detects only whole, base64- and hex-encoded values, and that the page's rule is broader.

findings.claim: The Windows bash wording does not match how the tests find bash; not run on Windows, reasoned from the code. README line 46 and lab.json tell a Windows learner to check `bash --version` for "the bash that comes with Git for Windows". Git for Windows' default install puts only its cmd folder on PATH, so in PowerShell or cmd that check either fails or runs a different bash (for example WSL's), although the tests would work: findBash (tests/behavior.mjs lines 55-64) locates Git's bin\bash.exe from git --exec-path, off PATH. A learner who follows the README check may wrongly conclude the prerequisite is missing, or trust a WSL bash the tests never use. Separately, a step with shell: sh is spawned as a bare `sh` (behavior.mjs line 127), which is not on a default Windows PATH, so such a step would fail there with an exit status of null instead of a clear message. Wheels for every pin exist for win_amd64: a pip dry-run with --platform win_amd64 --python-version 3.12 resolves all 14.
findings.recommendation: On Windows, tell the learner to check `git --version` and that Git for Windows is installed (the tests find its bash themselves), or to run `"C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe" --version`. In behavior.mjs, run `shell: sh` steps with the bash it found in POSIX mode (bash --posix -e), or report a clear problem when sh is missing. Record a Windows run locally before claiming windows in lab.json os.

findings.claim: The step runner's environment is narrower than a runner's, so some correct login steps fail test 6 with an unhelpful message. Reproduced: the README login plus a line appending LOGGED_IN=true to "$GITHUB_ENV" fails test 6 with only "exited with status 1 (bash -e stops the step at the first failing command)". GITHUB_ENV is unset, so the redirect fails, and unlike the stopped-before-login branch (tests/lab.mjs lines 421-425) the message omits the failing log line. GITHUB_OUTPUT, GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY and GITHUB_WORKSPACE are likewise unset. The same holds for writing to $GITHUB_OUTPUT before the login ("... stopped (exit status 1) before docker login ran: .../step.sh: line 1: : No such file or directory"). Also, username option parsing (optionValue, lab.mjs lines 393-399) reads -u="$U" as the value "=<user>" and fails test 6 with a message saying the username is not the secret's value. The docker CLI is believed to accept that shorthand form (pflag); not verified here. Neither shape is taught or on the README path; hence low.
findings.recommendation: In runStep, set GITHUB_ENV, GITHUB_OUTPUT, GITHUB_PATH and GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY to empty files in the temporary folder and GITHUB_WORKSPACE to the work folder. In the exited-with-status branch of ci-secret-refs, append the last log line as the earlier branch does. Optionally strip one leading '=' from a short-option value in optionValue.

findings.claim: The README timing is no longer honest for the loop-5 bytes, and the evidence behind it describes the loop-4 text-only lab. (1) coding-lab-timing.json line 21 derives phase 1 (5 minutes) from "README 969 words at 200 wpm = 4.8". The loop-5 README is 1212 words by wc -w; the 60a6b944 README is 969 by the same count. At the record's own rate that is about 6.1 minutes of reading, so phase 1 is about 7 minutes and S38 about 39, not the 37 that README line 32 and lab.json give. The typical path becomes about 58 minutes, so the 60-minute allowance covers about two failed reruns, not the four README lines 35-36 state. (2) coding-lab-timing.json line 8 says "No container engine, Python runtime or CI runner is used by this lab", and lines 14-15 and 72 give the one-time setup as about 3 minutes. README line 37 now says about 5 minutes, and setup now creates a Python venv and installs 14 packages (about 8 s on the critic's warm machine, but network-dependent). (3) coding-lab-solved-run.json is "solved at 2204f76c". Its toolchain.engine (line 13) and testScope (line 44) say Python is never executed and main.py is read as text, and it binds none of tests/behavior.mjs, service_behavior.py, setup_python.mjs or requirements.txt. The learner reads (1) in the README; (2) and (3) are evidence the timing and the solved-run gate rest on.
findings.recommendation: Either trim the README back toward the budgeted length (for example, move the Goal's and phase 6's how-the-tests-run detail into one short Testing note), or re-derive phase 1 from the current word count. Then update the S38 total, the typical minutes and the stated rerun allowance in README lines 32 and 35-36, lab.json minutes and coding-lab-timing.json together. Update the record's note and setup minutes to match README line 37, with a basis for the 5-minute figure. Re-record the solved run on the loop-5 bytes with Python and bash in the toolchain and the setup step in the procedure, then regenerate the module lock.
